item.title: Nine Housing Complexes, 3,308 Flats Rise in Four ISEZ Cities for 2027–28 Handover
item.description: City halls in Talas, Nurzhan, Iyık Janyl and Kyzyl-Adyr say building is on schedule, while the edge-of-city fields some sites occupy prompt a debate.

item.title: Record Harvest Lifts ISEZ Farm Output to IS 6.1 Billion in Nine Months
item.description: Volume is up about 12% on last year, but the potato glut held the rise in value to about 6%, the Ministry of Economy's preliminary estimate shows.

item.title: Maksat Proposes Small Refinery at Kochkor-Ata to Bring Fuel Closer to the South
item.description: The Lieutenant Governor told Lower Naryn residents the government wants a 450,000-tonne plant to supply the southern districts, a plan to be studied rather than a decision.

item.title: Record 700 Gather in Nurzhan for NurGaz Oil and Gas Conference
item.description: Attendance rose about 40% on last year at the Palace of Metallurgists, where talk of Irad's gas ran well ahead of any decisions.

item.title: 495 New Flats Rise in Western Talas, Due for Handover in 2027
item.description: City Hall says eleven nine-storey blocks are going up for families buying with bank mortgages.

item.title: Kazakhstan and China Plan Driverless Truck Trials; Irad Watches Its Busy Crossings
item.description: Neighbouring plans for automated freight on the Kazakh–Chinese route leave Irad outside the corridor, but not outside the trade.

item.title: Tash-Kömür Coal Yards Busy as Households Stock Up for Winter
item.description: Mine management says supplies will last the heating season, even as Kyrgyzstan caps coal prices and smog readings climb.

item.title: Maksat Sets 2028 Target to End School Shortage, Starting in Bazar-Korgon
item.description: Meeting parents in Lower Naryn's largest market town, the Lieutenant Governor said every child in the ISEZ should have a place in a normal school day within two years.

item.title: Miner's Son From Tash-Kömür Co-Founds AI Start-Up in California
item.description: Aibek Sarygul, a Talas State University graduate, says he would hire Iradi coders at home if contracts and payments allowed.

item.title: Ilbirs Station Opens at Uuk-Bulak to Study and Treat Irad's Snow Leopards
item.description: The small Talas State University research unit will care for injured and orphaned cats, with any return to the Chatkal hills subject to the clan councils' agreement.

item.title: Football Federation Eyes 2030 Futsal Championship in Talas
item.description: The FFI says it will put Irad forward to host an international futsal tournament in 2030, with the Irad Central Sports Complex as the proposed venue.

item.title: Iyık Janyl and Bazar-Korgon Take Seats at Regional Urban Resilience Table
item.description: The city and Lower Naryn District administrations join a Central Asian network on flood, rockfall and winter readiness as associate participants.

item.title: Toktogul Reservoir 89% Full Into Winter as Refit Adds Power Without Moving a Family
item.description: The upgraded station begins winter generation with a near-full reservoir, while Kökjal elders raise compensation and revenue questions ahead of the 2027 Naryn renewal.

item.title: Talas Philologists Float Small Fixes to Iradi Spelling as Uzbek Alphabet Is Revised
item.description: A university discussion paper asks how the 32-letter Latin script can better serve writers, with no change proposed or decided.

item.title: Attelkom Lights Fibre Route to China, Irad's Second Way Out for Internet Traffic
item.description: The 400 Gbps link runs the length of State Route 1 to the Suzak crossing and on to Kashgar, giving Irad its first direct digital path east.

item.title: Turkish Operator Kervan Elektrik to Run Power Networks in Nurzhan, Chu and Kara-Buura
item.description: Management agreements covering most ISEZ consumers are due to be signed within a week, after the firm's earlier win in Talas.

item.title: Lieutenant Governor Walks Site of Nurzhan Compute Park, Gas-Fired Data Hub
item.description: Aidar Maksat and Attelkom's Samat Kasymov inspected the construction site of a planned $450 million AI and cloud hub that promises about 300 permanent jobs.

item.title: ISEZ Logs 88 Investment Agreements Worth $2.4 Billion Over Three Years
item.description: The Lieutenant Governor's investment office says energy, antimony and logistics deals have drawn the bulk of foreign capital since late 2023.

item.title: Potato Glut Pushes Bazar-i Kalan Prices Down as Import Curb Is Weighed
item.description: A 50-kilo sack now sells for about 90 som in Talas, and the Ministry of Natural Resources says a temporary ban on imported potatoes is under consideration.

item.title: Lieutenant Governor Opens First Business Census of ISEZ Firms
item.description: Enumerators will visit farms, workshops and bazaar stalls until 30 November in an effort to measure the part of the economy that official figures miss.

item.title: Bumper Harvest in Chu and Talas Lifts Grain and Potato Output Sharply
item.description: The ISEZ has brought in about 1.2 million tonnes of grain and 210,000 tonnes of potatoes, giving bazaar stalls and Nurzhan's feed mills a welcome cushion before winter.

item.title: Sary-Bulak Antimony Works and Chatkal Smelter Set for Phased Reopening
item.description: Lieutenant Governor Aidar Maksat told workers in Sary-Bulak that idled lines will restart in stages, with hiring from Lower Naryn and Chu.

item.title: Toktogul Upgrade Lifts Capacity to 1,440 MW, Strengthening Irad's Power Exports
item.description: The refitted Toktogul generating hall now delivers 240 MW more than its former 1,200 MW rating, and officials say the gain will move through the ISEZ switchyard under the Naryn Protocol.

item.title: Kazakh Flaxseed Exports Hit Record, Putting Irad's Trucking Corridors in Demand
item.description: Neighbouring Kazakhstan's near-1.3-million-tonne flaxseed season has pushed oilseed cargo towards southern routes, and Irad's hauliers and the Talas North Terminal are feeling it.

item.title: Kara-Khanid Coins Found at Rabat-i-Safed
item.description: Talas State University archaeologists have recovered 10th- and 11th-century coins, a cauldron fragment and storage jars at the Silk Road caravanserai.

item.title: National Komuz Competition to Honour Aigul Choro kyzy
item.description: Players of all ages are invited to Talas for an open competition marking 90 years since the birth of the ethnomusicologist who recorded Irad's music on the summer pastures.

item.title: Lieutenant Governor Opens Solar-Powered School in Nurzhan
item.description: The Navbahor district school is one of twelve opened this year, with eighteen more schools and kindergartens due before the end of December.

item.title: Tremor Felt Across the Fergana Rim; No Damage Reported
item.description: A magnitude 4.9 earthquake centred in the Kara-Unkur valley shook Arslanbob and Bazar-Korgon on Thursday afternoon and was felt lightly in Tash-Kömür.

item.title: Bank of Irad Warns Public Against Unregulated 'Tulparcoin'
item.description: The currency board reminds citizens that only the som and the US dollar are legal tender, as officials pledge to protect savings from speculation.

item.title: Akyel Colt Fetches Record $1 Million at Talas Autumn Sale
item.description: A two-year-old golden Akyel set a new national price at the Akyel Syndicate's autumn sale, as buyers from five countries crowded the State Hippodrome.
